pages.text: A vespene vein's $(l)branches$() end underground in small pockets where vespene is taken $(l)by bucket$() only: no gas building stands there.$(br2)In some regions of the world a vein ends $(l)deep underground$() in a geyser of its own, far from the geysers on the surface: in a cave of natural shape, now and then with mineral crystals round it, and a $(l)great cave$() winds up to it from the surface. $(l)Mineral halls$() deep down have such a cave too.
